newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber mostly easier in soft market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber mostly easier in soft market.

text.p: Rubber futures ended mostly easier on Friday as weak prices in Japan depressed sentiment with the market seen slipping further next week, dealers said.
"The market took note of the fact that prices in Japan had come down quite a bit. Some inquiries in the market, however, kept the prices from sliding too much," a local rubber trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark March contract fell two yen to 132.5 while Kobe's March contract settled in after-hours trade at 131.7 from yesterday's close of 134.3.
"The market remained very soft because of ample supplies," another trader said.
"I don't see the situation changing next week. I believe we will still have a weak market," one dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 123.50-124.50 U.S. cents a kg from 124.50 cents.
December RSS1 was seen unchanged at 177.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg.
December TSR20 was seen at 173.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg against the previous 174.50 cents.
